posts.title: GULF cafe

copy.default:
One thing I want more of while building everything else:

More moments like this.

Coffee with my partner. Trying something new. Slowing down enough to actually enjoy where I am.

I can be very forward-focused. The next move. The next target. The next opportunity. The next level.

Ambition is good. But I do not want to become so obsessed with the future that I stop experiencing the present properly.

Build seriously. Care deeply. Work hard.

But make room for good coffee, good company and new experiences too.

23,188 steps.

Canal walk first. Then Darwen Tower. Then the celebratory photo at the top.

A lot of the things that make you proud afterwards do not feel particularly glamorous while you are doing them.

It is just step after step after step.

No dramatic breakthrough. Just movement.

Building feels similar sometimes.

People see the milestone. They rarely see all the ordinary reps underneath it.

Keep walking. Keep building.

posts.title: Porsche in Manchester

copy.default:
Spotted a gorgeous Porsche in Manchester and had one of those moments where ambition and humour meet in the middle.

I was admiring the car, but also very aware I was still just a guy in the street having a laugh.

I actually like this stage of life.

Wanting more without pretending I already have it.

I do want a big life. Success. Freedom. Financial security. Things I genuinely enjoy.

But I also want to enjoy becoming the person who gets there.

posts.title: Thailand birthday

copy.default:
Thailand, July 2025.

One thing travelling keeps teaching me is how much bigger life is than whatever feels urgent in the moment.

Work, pressure and goals can make your world feel very narrow.

Then you go somewhere new and your perspective stretches again.

Different environment. Different pace. Different reminders of what is possible.

That is part of why I value travel so much.

Sometimes getting out of your usual environment helps you come back thinking bigger.

posts.title: Amsterdam Capri-Sun

copy.default:
I have a feeling I am going to miss this stage one day.

Not because everything is easy. It is not.

But because so much is still unwritten.

I do not know exactly how big the business becomes. I do not know which opportunities will matter most. I do not know who I will meet along the way.

And I actually like that.

My job is just to keep giving myself more chances for the right things to happen.

Apparently with a Capri-Sun in hand.

posts.title: Manchester Chinatown

copy.default:
One thing I do not want entrepreneurship to do is make my world smaller.

Laptop. Phone. Emails. Calls. Repeat.

There is always another thing I could be doing.

But I also want more places, more people, more conversations and more experiences.

Because building a good business means very little to me if I accidentally build a boring life around it.

I want both.

posts.title: Amsterdam ice cream

copy.default:
Building something can make you permanently focused on the next thing.

Next client. Next target. Next idea. Next version of yourself.

I am definitely guilty of it.

But I do not want to spend years building the life I want and forget to actually live any of it on the way.

Build hard. Take the opportunities. Raise the standard.

But also go to Amsterdam and get the ice cream.

There will still be work tomorrow.

posts.title: G-Wagon aspiration

copy.default:
I can stand next to a G-Wagon for a photo in 10 seconds.

I cannot fake consistent £2.5k weeks.

That is the thing I am actually trying to build right now.

Francis can pick up the phone and book a business owner.

I can take the call.

We can run the Revenue Recovery Check.

We can build the follow-up system.

But none of that matters because it exists on a diagram.

It matters when it produces revenue, then produces revenue again.

That is the gap I am trying to close.

I do not want one good week I can screenshot and call momentum.

I want £2.5k to stop feeling like a good week and start feeling like what the business does.

We are not there yet.

And that is why this photo is useful to me in a completely different way than “manifest the car”.

It is easy to look at the visible outcome and skip over the boring repeatability underneath it.

The car can wait.

I want the boring weeks first.

posts.title: I would not read my own posts

copy.default:
I read back the posts I had lined up for this week and realised something slightly embarrassing.

I would not stop to read any of them.

They were not wrong.
They were not badly written.
They were worse.

Forgettable.

Nice photo.
Neat lesson.
Founder-sounding ending.

You could have swapped my name for almost anyone else's and nothing would have changed.

That bothered me more than a post flopping.

Because I do not want to spend the next year documenting a version of building Triple Two Emails that sounds cleaner, wiser or more certain than the actual thing.

The actual thing right now is messier.

I am trying to make £2.5k weeks repeat.

I am learning what Francis can own and what still needs me.

I am taking calls that might turn into something and others that will not.

I am changing my mind on things I was convinced about a week ago.

Some ideas work.

Some are shit.

That is the part worth documenting.

So I changed the standard.

If there is not a real event, number, tension, mistake or decision underneath the post, I do not want it.

I would rather post less and have something worth remembering than stay “consistent” with things I would not read myself.

The business is still being figured out.

The content should be allowed to look like it.
